title: Set the total budget and who contributes
details: Put the amounts in the Calculator. Talk openly with both sets of parents about what each will cover.

title: Make the big guest list, by family
details: The list decides the venue and the budget. Put everyone on it now and cut later. Note which side each family is on.

title: Pick 2–3 possible dates
details: Check the fasting periods (no religious weddings during fasts), holidays and important family dates.

title: Choose your godparents
details: Ask them early: the date has to work for them too.

title: Visit venues and ask for quotes
details: Ask for the full menu, what the price includes (drinks, cake, decor), the service charge, the closing time, the deposit and the payment deadlines.

title: Book the venue and sign the contract
details: Ask about: your own stage or the band's · how many waiters and what an extra one costs · bar and bartender · starters on arrival · changing room for the couple and the band · menus for kids and staff · when the final guest count is due.

title: Book the church
details: In summer, some parishes are booked a year ahead.

title: Book the band or DJ
details: Ask for the technical rider and check it with the venue: stage, power, changing room, a table for the band.

title: Book the photographer and videographer
details: Ask what is included: a separate photo session, the civil ceremony, an album, the delivery time.

title: Decide whether to hire a planner or a day-of coordinator
details: A day-of coordinator costs less and spares you from chasing vendors on the day.

title: Send save the dates
details: Especially to guests from other cities or abroad.

title: Make a list of accommodation near the venue
details: Name, price, distance to the venue and a link. Send it to guests coming from other cities.

title: Choose the wedding dress
details: Ask about the number of fittings and the delivery time. Some dresses take 4–6 months.

title: Book the florist and decor
details: The bride's and the godmother's bouquets, boutonnieres, the couple's table arrangement, the table centerpieces, the ceremony candles.

title: Book the cake and candy bar
details: Cake design, topper, cake boxes, who brings it and what time it is set up.

title: Choose the photo booth or magic mirror
Decide what to do for the civil ceremony
details: Only at the town hall, or a small party too? If you have a party, add it separately in the Calculator.

title: Decide who organises the bachelor and bachelorette parties
Order the invitations
details: Count by family, not by person. Order 5–10 extra.

title: Order the wedding rings
details: Engraving can take 2–4 weeks.

title: Choose the groom's suit
details: Plus shoes, shirt, cufflinks, watch.

title: Choose the hair and makeup and book the trial
details: Ask whether they come to your home or the hotel, and what it costs for the mothers and bridesmaids.

title: Plan the first dance and special moments with the band
details: The first dance, the father–bride moment, the cake, the bouquet toss, the genres you want and the ones you don't.

title: Take dance lessons (optional)
Prepare an RSVP form
details: Ask: coming or not, who they bring, dietary restrictions (vegetarian, no pork, no fish), kids, whether they need accommodation.

title: Plan the honeymoon
details: Check passports, travel insurance and bookings.

title: Arrange guest transport, if needed
details: A coach from the church to the venue or from the hotel to the venue. Set the departure time and place.

title: Send the invitations
details: Note who you sent them to and who answers for each family.

title: Find out which documents the town hall requires for the civil ceremony
details: The list differs from one town hall to another. Ask about booking and the fee too.

title: Order the wedding favours
Buy the accessories
details: Shoes (and a spare, flat pair), jewellery, veil, ring pillow, flower petal basket.

title: Make a guest guide
details: The day's schedule, addresses, parking, accommodation, dress code. A PDF or a page on a website.

title: Book the wedding-day photo session
details: The location, the time, and whether a permit is needed (some parks and museums ask for one).

title: Make the photo shot list for the photographer
details: The photos you absolutely want and the groups: each side's family, the godparents, friends.

title: Prepare the design for menus, the gift list, envelopes and table numbers
details: The gift list and envelopes need the final table list. Leave them for last.

title: Ask the restaurant for the run sheet
details: The time each course is served, the band's breaks, the cake.

title: Call guests who haven't replied
details: Split the list: each of you calls your own people.

title: Plan the seating
details: Start with the head table and family. Keep couples and families at the same table. Note how many seats each table has.

title: Get the tests for the premarital certificate
details: The certificate is valid for a short time (usually 14 days). Book the tests so it is still valid when you file.

title: Collect the special menus by table
details: Vegetarian, no pork, no fish, kids, staff. The restaurant wants the list with each person's name and table.

title: File the paperwork with the civil registry
details: The marriage declaration is filed at least 10 days before the ceremony. Check the exact deadline at your town hall.

title: Final fitting for the dress and suit
Make the day's schedule, hour by hour
details: Makeup, hair, getting ready, photos, church, arrival at the restaurant, entrances, the cake. Send it to each vendor with their arrival time.

title: Print the gift list, menus, envelopes and table numbers
Prepare the wedding-day payments
details: One envelope per vendor, with the amount and their name, and a trusted person to hand them out.

title: Pack the emergency kit
details: Safety pins, needle and thread, deodorant, powder, lipstick, perfume, hairpins, plasters, tissues, spare shoes.

title: Tell the restaurant the final guest count
details: With the table list, the special menus and the number of seats at each table.

title: Confirm the arrival time with each vendor
details: Band, photo and video, florist, candy bar, photo booth, hostess, coach.

title: Prepare the hostess list and the gift box
Pack what you are taking to the venue
details: Favours, table numbers, gift list, ring pillow, fans, fairy lights, the ribbon for the bouquet toss, cases of water.

title: Pick up the dress and suit
Prepare the getting-ready rooms and the accommodation
details: Water in the rooms, the getting-ready room tidy and cool, something to eat in the morning.

title: Hand the payment envelopes to the person in charge
Give the rings to the godparents
Check the drinks for getting ready
details: Glasses for wine and prosecco, ice buckets, water and soft drinks in cans or 0.5 l bottles.

title: Note down each guest's gift
details: While it is fresh, by family. It will help you at their events.

title: Make the final payments to vendors
Return what you rented or borrowed
Thank your guests and godparents
Update your documents, if you changed your name
details: First the ID card, then the passport, the driving licence and the bank.

title: Receive the photos and the film
details: Check the delivery time in the contract.
